stem.text: The function h is continuous and \( h(t) > 0 \) for all t. Let \( g(x) = \int_{0}^{x} 3\left(t - 1\right)\left(t - 8\right)h(t)\,dt \) for \( 0 < x < 7 \). Find the value of x in \( 0 < x < 7 \) at which g has a critical point, and determine whether g has a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither there. Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: At x = 1 only; g has a relative maximum there because g' changes from positive to negative at x = 1.

worked_solution.text: \( g'(x) \) is \( 3\left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 8\right) \) times \( h(x) \), which is positive, so \( g'(x) = 0 \) only where \( 3\left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 8\right) = 0 \), at x = 1 and x = 8.
Only x = 1 lies in \( 0 < x < 7 \); x = 8 is greater than every x in the range.
On the range the factor \( \left(x - 8\right) \) keeps one sign, so g' changes from positive to negative at x = 1, and g has a relative maximum there.

options.label: At x = 1 only; g has a relative maximum there because g' changes from positive to negative at x = 1.
At x = 1 only; g has neither there because g' stays close to 0 on both sides of x = 1.
options.derivation: the point classified by the size of the derivative nearby rather than by whether its sign changes

options.label: At x = 1 only; g has a relative minimum there because g' changes from positive to negative at x = 1.
options.derivation: the direction of the sign change read the wrong way round in the classification

options.label: At x = 1 and x = 8; g has a relative maximum at x = 1 and a relative minimum at x = 8 because g' changes sign at each.
options.derivation: the zero x = 8 of the derivative kept although it lies outside the stated range
